profile.campus: Aurora, Kane/DuPage County, Illinois (CyrusOne CHI1-CHI3 campus)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own campus page, the Aurora, Illinois (CHI1-CHI3) campus spans 2705-2905 Diehl Rd, Aurora, IL 60502, publishing 450,000 sq ft and 114 MW of total IT capacity across three buildings.

Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states the company completed an acquisition of a CME Group data center in Aurora in March 2016 (this is the original CHI1 building, formerly the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's own facility, purchased for roughly $130 million with CME Group continuing to run its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease) and began construction of a 425,000 sq ft expansion facility there; CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, and was taken private in a roughly $15 billion deal when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it, closing March 2022.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.
profile.facility_note: CyrusOne CHI1-CHI3, Aurora, Illinois: a three-building, 450,000 sq ft / 114MW campus anchored by the original CME Group-acquired facility.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus publishes 114 MW of IT capacity, making it the largest single disclosed facility in Illinois and representing 48 percent of the state's published data center power.

At 114 MW and assuming conservative mixed-workload density, the campus could host roughly 2,280 H100 GPUs if fully deployed for AI training. The actual number depends on tenant mix, which the operator does not disclose. This capacity is material but insufficient for the largest training clusters, which typically require colocation of multiple facilities or dedicated infrastructure.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities, but only six publish capacity figures. The remaining 38 facilities report no power metrics, meaning actual state capacity is substantially higher than the 236 MW of published figures. The Aurora campus dominates disclosed capacity, but this reflects reporting opacity rather than technical dominance.

The campus matters to AI infrastructure primarily as a local constraint on the Chicago metro region. Whether it becomes central to AI scaling depends on three unknowns the data does not cover: total grid supply available to the site, what fraction of the 114 MW the operator allocates to AI versus other workloads, and whether CyrusOne publishes additional capacity figures that are not yet sourced.
